source.authorityName: School examination paper (school not named); obtained from icseboard.org, originally from icseonline.com
source.notes: ICSE Std. IX school final term examination paper (school not named). Header prints 'Final Term Examination 2017-2018', 'Std. : IX', 'Subject : CHEMISTRY', 'Full Marks : 80', 'Time : 2 hrs.+15 mins.' (135 minutes). examYear 2018 is the later year of the printed academic year 2017-2018. Section A (40 marks, 'Attempt All The Questions') is Question I with eight lettered groups a)-h), each printed with one group total [5]; each group is kept as one entry with that total. Section B ('Attempt any four') prints Questions 2-7 (10 marks each), so the pack's marks total (100) exceeds 80; Section B parts carry printed marks and are split where marked. Question 2 prints an unlettered item 'i)' with its own [2] after part d); it is stored as part '(i)'. Question 3 prints two parts labelled 'b)'; the second (Group 1, [5]) is stored as part '(b) second'. Several items (ammonia, hydrogen chloride, metallurgy of aluminium, analysis with ammonium hydroxide) are Class X ICSE topics with no matching Class IX chapter and have chapter null. The PDF has no text layer (watermark only); text was OCRed with RapidOCR and corrected against the page images (the page images are typeset, clean scans). No answer key is printed; no official answers exist.
source.usage: School examination paper published on icseboard.org (originally icseonline.com); question text reproduced for study with attribution and a link to where it was obtained. Figures are not reproduced.

questions.sectionTitle: Section A : 40 Marks Attempt All The Questions
questions.text:
Give one word for the following :
(i) The largest atom in the third period
(ii) A bond formed by the transfer of electrons
(iii) Property of a metal by virtue of which it can be beaten into thin sheets
(iv) The experiment which demonstrates high solubility of hydrogen chloride gas.
(v) A formula which shows the simplest whole number ratio
extractionIssues: Group of five one-word items under one printed total [5]; items span several chapters

questions.sectionTitle: Section A : 40 Marks Attempt All The Questions
questions.text:
Write fully balanced chemical equation for each of the following reactions :
(i) Dilute sulphuric acid is added to Iron
(ii) Heating of Aluminium hydroxide
(iii) Ammonia is passed over heated lead oxide
(iv) Water is reacted with Magnesium nitride
(v) Hydrogen chloride is reacted with ammonia

questions.sectionTitle: Section A : 40 Marks Attempt All The Questions
questions.text:
Solve the following :
(i) What volume of oxygen would be required for the complete combustion of 100 litres of ethane according to the following equation ?
2C2H6 + 7O2 ⟶ 4CO2 + 6H2O
(ii) Calculate the percentage composition of water in FeSO4.7H2O.
[Fe=56, S=32, 0=16, H=l]
extractionIssues: Atomic masses printed as '0=16, H=l' (kept as printed)

questions.sectionTitle: Section A : 40 Marks Attempt All The Questions
questions.text:
Choose the appropriate answer :
(i) An alkaline earth metal is :
A. Palladium B. Calcium C. Lead D. Copper
(ii) The number of electrons present in the valence shell of an halogen
A. 1 B. 2 C. 5 D. 7
(iii) The molecule containing triple covalent bond is :
A. Ammonia B. Methane C. Water D. Nitrogen
(iv) The number of atoms present in one molecule of an element is called its:
A. Molecular number B. Atomic number C. Avogadro's number D. Atomicity
(v) Hydrogen chloride gas is dried by:
A. Dilute sulphuric acid B. Concentrated nitric acid C. Quick lime D. Concentrated sulphuric acid.
extractionIssues: Group of five MCQs under one printed total [5]; options kept inside the text

questions.sectionTitle: Section A : 40 Marks Attempt All The Questions
questions.text:
Identify the gas in each of the following cases :
i) A colourless gas which forms an explosive mixture with air and water is the only product of combustion
(ii) A colourless gas having the smell of burnt Sulphur
(iii) A colourless gas that turns lead acetate paper black
(iv) The gas produced when excess ammonia reacts with chlorine
(v) The gas produced when concentrated sulphuric acid reacts with sodium chloride

questions.sectionTitle: Section A : 40 Marks Attempt All The Questions
questions.text:
Answer the following :
i) Name the chief ore of aluminium
ii) Name the process used to concentrate the above-mentioned ore
iii) Give cathode and anode reactions involved in the extraction of aluminium from its above mentioned ore.
iv) Name the process used for the concentration of Zinc blende
extractionIssues: Only four items printed under the group total [5]

questions.sectionTitle: Section A : 40 Marks Attempt All The Questions
questions.text:
Fill in the blanks from the choices given below :
i) In covalent compounds, the bond is formed due to the ________ (sharing, transfer) of electrons.
ii) Electrovalent compounds have a ________ (low, high) boiling point.
iii) The ratio of certain mass of a gas or vapour to the mass of same volume of hydrogen is its ________ (atomicity / vapour density)
iv) Across a period, the ionization potential ________ (increases, decreases, remains same)
v) Down the group, electron affinity ________ (increases, decreases, remain same)

questions.sectionTitle: Section A : 40 Marks Attempt All The Questions
questions.text:
Arrange as directed:
(i) Mg2+, Mg, Mg+ (increasing size)
(ii) Cl, F, I, Br (increasing electronegativity)
(iii) Na, Rb, Li, Cs (increasing metallic character)
(iv) B, Li, Be (increasing valency)
(v) Ar, He, Ne (increasing order of electron shells)
Ammonia gas catches fire when burnt in the atmosphere of oxygen. What do you observe when ammonia burns in air ?
Write a balanced equation for the combustion of ammonia in oxygen.

Ammonia is catalytically oxidized with oxygen.
i) Name the catalyst.
ii) Write a balanced chemical equation for the catalytic oxidation of ammonia.
iii) Name the industrial process which starts with the catalytic oxidation of ammonia.
iv) Name the drying agent used in the laboratory preparation of ammonia.

An element 'X' has 2 electrons in the outermost shell of its atom and combines with an element Y having seven electrons in the outermost shell of its atom.
i) Write the formula of the compound formed
ii) What type of bond is formed between X & Y ?

When the ore of aluminium is treated with sodium hydroxide solution, what happens to :
A) Aluminium oxide B) Iron (III) oxide
extractionIssues: Printed as an unlettered item 'i)' with its own [2] after part d)

questions.text:

i) protecting iron from rusting
ii) making thin foils for packaging industry
iii) the construction of machinery

With reference to the industrial preparation of ammonia, answer the following questions :
i) Name the industrial method.
ii) Name the catalyst used.
iii) Write balanced chemical reaction for ans 4(b)(i)
iv) What is the role of promoter in this reaction?

Write the formula of the following compounds :
i) Aluminium hydroxide ii) Potassium permanganate iii) Sodium meta aluminate

Identify the salts insoluble in water :
Barium sulphate, Silver nitrate, Lead sulphate, Aluminium sulphate, Ferrous sulphide, Mercury (II) sulphate.

A compound X has the following percentage composition: Carbon = 26.7%, oxygen = 71.1% and hydrogen = 2.2%
A. Determine the empirical formula.
B. Determine the molecular formula of X, it its relative molecular weight is 90.

i) The anode is replaced periodically. Why ?
ii) Coke is sprinkled over the electrolyte. Give reasons.

In the laboratory preparation of HCl :
i) Why is concentrated nitric acid not used ?
ii) How is HCl gas collected? Give reasons.
iii) Why is the temperature maintained below 200°C ?

In the laboratory preparation of Ammonia :
i) Explain why a higher ratio of calcium hydroxide used.
ii) The flask in which the reaction occurs is kept inclined. Why ?
iii) Why is sodium hydroxide not used for the above purpose ?
